findings.bites_when: The first Act-emitting behaviour commit (core-model step 4) writes the ring through updateSlice or set_state_slice, or any HUD/notebook reader calls get() per frame; also createInitialWorldState and loadFromSlot do toSnapshot+fromSnapshot (2 more clones of every slice).
findings.disconfirm: Checked whether any production code uses slices yet: no (grep finds only SimulationCoordinator save/load and the reducer), so cost is zero today; also checked entities/props maps: only a shallow O(entities) spread per effect (1000 effects x 300 entities = 4.5 ms) and untouched entities keep identity, so those are fine. Numbers are on this dev machine, not the 2019 i7 (likely 1.5-2x slower).
findings.recommendation: Make slices frozen-on-write, shared-on-read: withSlice does one deepFreeze (skip if already frozen) and get() returns the frozen reference; updaters must return new values (spread/concat), which the type already encourages via readonly. For the Act ring use a chunked persistent structure: array of fixed 256-row frozen chunks plus a head chunk, so append copies at most one chunk; Observation as Record<holderId, frozen rows> so a write touches one holder. Drop the redundant defineStateSlice call in set_state_slice. toSnapshot can return the frozen refs without cloning.
findings.ignore_cost: The Act ring is built on a store that makes every append cost a frame, and the 'write per watch' workaround gets baked into the model.

findings.disconfirm: Looked for any consumer of StateSliceRegistry in src: only domain/index.ts re-exports it; no production defineStateSlice call exists outside the reducer. So nothing is broken yet; this is a seam gap, not a live bug.
findings.recommendation: Extend StateSliceKey with an optional Zod schema and integer version plus an optional migrate(old, fromVersion); make set_state_slice resolve through the registry (unknown id -> rejection) and validate on write in dev/eval; reject non-plain-JSON values (Map/Set/Date/function) in defineStateSlice/withSlice. Slice values then are guaranteed save-safe.
findings.ignore_cost: Every pack slice ships with no save migration path, and a renamed field silently reads as undefined mid-game.

findings.claim: SeededRandom does not scramble its seed, so small seeds give strongly non-uniform first draws (the coordinator default seed 1 yields first nextFloat 6.3e-5; 16% of seeds 1..1000 have a first float < 0.01 vs ~1% expected), seeds 0, 2^32 and 0x6d2b79f5 alias to one stream, and the single mutable stream lives outside WorldState with no fork/derive API, so any added roll shifts every later roll.

findings.bites_when: The first probabilistic rule lands (interception risk, detection roll, storyteller deck shuffle) and a human-chosen seed such as 1, 2, 42 is used: the first roll of the run is near 0 and 'roll < risk' triggers on every small seed. Also bites the day a second subsystem draws from the shared stream.
findings.disconfirm: Checked whether anything rolls today: grep for nextFloat/nextInt/choose in src finds no caller (only getRng accessor), so nothing is skewed yet. Checked zero-seed handling: it is handled (fixed default), and the nextInt rejection sampling is correct.
findings.recommendation: Run the seed through splitmix32 (or mulberry32 init) in the constructor, and keep Xorshift only as the stepper. Add a pure counter-based roll: rollFloat(worldSeed, streamKey, counter) = hash32(seed ^ hash(streamKey), counter), where counter is actId or watch; put worldSeed in WorldState (immutable) so replay needs seed + effect log, not a threaded generator. Keep SeededRandom for sequential local use only.
findings.ignore_cost: Every saved run's random stream is pinned to the current weak seeding, and changing it later invalidates all golden/eval fixtures.

findings.claim: The per-entity stimulus cap evicts the oldest stimulus regardless of importance and stimulusId is never deduplicated, so 32 ambient chatter stimuli silently delete an earlier player-caused alarm, and a replayed effect enqueues the same stimulus twice.

findings.claim: Reducer tests prove single-path happy cases only: nothing asserts input non-mutation (no frozen inputs), the stimulus and audio caps, duplicate/unknown ids, effect-order dependence, schema-versus-type parity, or SeededRandom golden values, so the determinism the whole replay story depends on is checked only as 'two runs agree with each other'.
findings.bites_when: Now: someone changes the Xorshift constants, clamp order or cap logic and every test still passes while saved runs and eval fixtures diverge.
findings.disconfirm: Checked the other domain test files and the application SimulationCoordinator test for caps and unknown ids: only one set_state_slice use (coordinator test 439) and no cap tests.
findings.recommendation: Add: (1) golden vector for SeededRandom (seed 42 -> first 5 uint32); (2) a helper that deepFreezes WorldState and effects then runs every effect type; (3) cap tests for stimuli/audio; (4) a seeded random-batch replay test that applies the same effect list twice and compares JSON; (5) a type-level test that each WorldEffect variant is covered by a reducer test via an exhaustive record of fixtures.
findings.ignore_cost: Determinism regressions are caught late, in eval drift, not in the 3 s unit suite.

keep.claim: The reducer is genuinely pure and structurally shared: every case spreads, untouched entities keep identity, batches are all-or-nothing, and entities/props maps are shallow-copied only (1000 effects over 300 entities = 4.5 ms). Protect this; do not 'fix' it with deep clones.

Exhaustiveness of the effect union is compiler-enforced (switch without default under strict return checking, discriminatedUnion parse before apply), and the prototype-pollution guard on prop patches is correct.

unconsidered_routes.title: Stateless counter-based rolls instead of threaded generators
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Replace the shared stateful SeededRandom with a pure roll(worldSeed, streamKey, counter) hash (splitmix/murmur finalizer). Streams are keyed by subsystem plus actId/watch, so adding a roll in one subsystem never moves another, and replay needs only seed plus the effect log. Keep the class for local sequential helpers.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Counter-based RNGs (Philox, SplitMix); Dwarf Fortress/Caves of Qud per-purpose seeded streams; Hades' per-system seeded RNG
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Removes rngState from the save envelope and the coordinator-held generator; worldSeed joins WorldState.

unconsidered_routes.title: Chunked persistent log for the Act ring and Observation table
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Store the ring as an array of frozen 256-row chunks with a head chunk and a base index; append copies only the head. Observation rows are keyed by holderId so a write replaces one frozen bucket. Reads return frozen references (no clone), writes freeze once.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Persistent vectors (Clojure/Immer structural sharing), event-sourced log segments
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Replaces structuredClone-per-get/set in StateSliceStore with freeze-on-write; makes 'bounded ring' a chunk drop rather than a slice() copy.

unconsidered_routes.title: Reducer returns outcomes, application layer owns the envelope
unconsidered_routes.proposal: applyWorldEffects(state, Envelope[]) where Envelope = {effect, actorId?, causeActId?}; the reducer returns outcomes (applied/rejected+reason) and stamps causeActId onto emitted audio cues, scars and stimuli. The 17 variants stay untouched because the envelope wraps rather than extends them.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Redux-style action meta fields; command/result pattern in Caves of Qud's event system
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Changes the return type once; replaces dispatchEffects options.actorId (telemetry only) with state-visible provenance.

readiness.envelope: Yes. WorldEffect is a Zod discriminatedUnion; applySingleWorldEffect(state, effect) takes the parsed effect, so a wrapper {effect, actorId, causeActId} can be unwrapped in applyWorldEffects with no variant change. Seam: the loop at WorldEffectReducer.ts:484-488 and DispatchEffectsOptions.actorId already carried to telemetry. Obstacles: appliedEffects is typed ReadonlyArray<WorldEffect> and consumed by inferEffectTelemetryCategory; cause stamping needs the reducer cases that create records (scars, audio cues, stimuli) to accept a cause param.
readiness.slices: Mechanically yes (defineStateSlice + set_state_slice), practically not until S3B-01 (clone cost) and S3B-02 (no schema/version/registry check) are fixed. Also the save path enumerates WorldState fields by hand in SimulationCoordinator.saveToSlot/loadFromSlot and a hand-written isSerializedWorldStateSnapshot guard, so any new top-level field (elapsedWatches) must be added in ~4 places and an old save loads it as undefined.
readiness.rejection: Not without a result-type change (S3B-05): outcome channel absent; throws at lines 61, 72, 398, 403.
readiness.advance_watches: Add elapsedWatches to WorldState (hand interface at WorldState.ts:140-156, createInitialWorldState, coordinator save/load) and a new effect variant; sits beside advance_orbital_pass, whose ticksInCurrentPhase is the only existing tick-unit counter and should fold into it. It must run before any stimulus/presence resolution in a batch since ordering within a batch is strictly sequential; stimuli keep readyAtElapsedSeconds (real seconds) so their fate across a watch jump (S2-11) needs an explicit rule, because enqueue computes readiness from elapsedSimulationSeconds only.
